title: Trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets
statement: For $n\geq0$ let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with $\Delta[n]_k$ the set of order-preserving maps $[k]\to[n]$ and $\Delta[n](\varphi)(\alpha)=\alpha\circ\varphi$, and let $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial subset of the non-surjective maps $[k]\to[n]$ (so $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty). A morphism $p:X\to Y$ of simplicial sets is a *trivial Kan fibration* if $p_0:X_0\to Y_0$ is surjective and for every $n\geq1$ and every pair of morphisms $a:\partial\Delta[n]\to X$, $b:\Delta[n]\to Y$ with $p\circ a=b|_{\partial\Delta[n]}$ there is a morphism $c:\Delta[n]\to X$ with $c|_{\partial\Delta[n]}=a$ and $p\circ c=b$.
